title: CyberAlchemy Knowledge Exchange Protocol Product Thesis
problem: Knowledge can be copied without preserving provenance, originator continuity, permission, encrypted delivery evidence, or the rules that govern later sharing.
value_proposition: The protocol lets one stable identity add another as co-owner of an exact encrypted knowledge-artifact version while retaining originator membership and producing bounded delivery evidence.
value_mechanism: Bind an immutable artifact version and policy to external content-addressed ciphertext, authorize an owner-set expansion, issue a recipient-specific key envelope, and record the recipient's signed acknowledgement.
boundaries: A remains a co-owner when B is added
plaintext and content keys remain outside public protocol state
the protocol does not custody the encrypted artifact
stable identity remains distinct from signing and encryption keys
reissue does not change ownership or economic state
SOL, licensing, royalties, reputation, publication, release, and deployment are excluded
hypotheses: signed owner-set expansion plus recipient-bound encrypted delivery creates a useful knowledge-sharing event
a stable identity can support safe lost-key reissue without changing ownership
separating compromised-key rotation into a new encryption epoch avoids false revocation claims
evidence_routes: lost-key reissue and compromised-key epoch negative tests
counterevidence_routes: identity cannot survive key replacement safely
owner membership and decryptable access cannot be distinguished
external ciphertext availability makes the proof unusable
a simpler mechanism preserves the same boundaries
revision_criteria: the first proof violates a first-order principle
key reissue silently changes ownership or policy
the model requires plaintext or a content key in public state
evidence cannot distinguish authorization from successful decryption
owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 Knowledge Exchange Protocol product owner

challenge_route: Challenge product meaning through the CyberAlchemy v2 Knowledge Exchange Protocol product owner; challenge capability shape through the CyberAlchemy v2 capability owner; challenge cryptography through an independent security owner; challenge implementation evidence through the future Solana realization owner.
